title: WhatsApp Embedded Signup v4 Rescue
one_liner: Fixed-scope migration and validation sprint for SaaS products, agencies and messaging platforms whose WhatsApp customer-onboarding flow still depends on Meta Embedded Signup v2/v3 before the 2026-10-15 retirement.
buyer: Small and mid-sized SaaS products, WhatsApp automation vendors, agencies and internal platforms that onboard customer WhatsApp Business accounts through Meta Embedded Signup and do not have spare Meta-platform engineering capacity.

pain.description: Meta retires Embedded Signup v2/v3 on 2026-10-15. An affected integration can keep serving existing senders while silently losing the ability to onboard new customers. Migration is not only a version-string change: v4 uses Facebook Login for Business configurations and requires end-to-end validation of permissions, callbacks, token exchange and webhooks.

observable_targeting.method: Public GitHub code search can expose repositories that reference WhatsApp Embedded Signup, FB.login and explicit v3/legacy feature configuration, allowing target discovery without paid ads or private data.
observations: Public code search on 2026-09-14 returned multiple active repositories implementing WhatsApp Embedded Signup.
At least one surfaced repository explicitly documents signup_version '3' and raw legacy extras.featureType handling.
Other surfaced projects contain FB.login-based WhatsApp onboarding code that can be inspected manually before any outreach.
This creates an unusually cheap acquisition path: detect legacy implementation -> verify repository/project -> contact only the maintainer/business where a credible commercial buyer exists.

findings: Twilio publishes a detailed migration guide and estimates the change at a couple of hours to one week depending on configuration, validating non-trivial implementation effort.
Search results contain many migration guides and vendors discussing the deadline, but no obvious dominant low-cost fixed-scope independent migration service surfaced in this check.
The main substitute is an internal developer following Meta/Twilio documentation, so the offer must sell speed, testing and deadline risk reduction rather than information.
competitive_validation.risk: Technically capable targets may prefer to migrate internally; generic educational content has near-zero willingness to pay.

offer.name: Embedded Signup v4 Rescue Sprint
scope: Identify current Embedded Signup version and legacy feature dependencies
Produce exact migration map to v4 configuration-driven flow
Patch or provide patch-ready code for the onboarding entry point
Validate callback, authorization-code exchange and required identifiers
Validate webhook delivery and Coexistence path when applicable
Provide rollback/checklist evidence before production cutover
offer.pricing_note: Use fixed scope after repository/config review. Do not promise App Review approval or Meta-side turnaround times.

validation.next_test: Build a list of 10-20 commercially plausible targets whose public code or documentation still shows legacy Embedded Signup implementation, then look for at least one explicit paid-interest signal before building a landing page.
validation.promotion_gate: At least one credible buyer asks for migration help, a quote, or a paid implementation discussion.

decision.reason: Hard deadline + high-value B2B failure mode + targets can be found from public implementation evidence. The remaining unknown is willingness to pay rather than existence of the technical problem.
